topics.name: Nerve Injury and Regeneration
topics.blurb: Classification, pathophysiology, and timing principles for traumatic peripheral nerve injury.

topics.name: Electrodiagnostics and Nerve Imaging
topics.blurb: EMG/NCS interpretation, denervation timing, and advanced nerve imaging.

topics.name: Entrapment Neuropathies
topics.blurb: Compressive mononeuropathies of the upper and lower extremity.

topics.name: Brachial Plexus Injury and Reconstruction
topics.blurb: Adult and obstetric plexus injury patterns, localization, and reconstructive transfers.

topics.name: Nerve Repair and Grafting Techniques
topics.blurb: Operative principles of neurorrhaphy, grafting, and reconstruction substrates.

topics.name: Peripheral Nerve Tumors
topics.blurb: Benign and malignant nerve sheath tumors and tumor-like lesions.

topics.name: Peripheral Nerve Differentials
topics.blurb: Confusable inflammatory, radicular, and mononeuropathic presentations.

concepts.name: Seddon classification
concepts.blurb: Three-tier injury scheme (neurapraxia, axonotmesis, neurotmesis) predicting spontaneous recovery potential.
acgme: Peripheral Nerve Injury - Sunderland or Seddon Classification

concepts.name: Sunderland classification
concepts.blurb: Five-degree scheme grading which connective layers are disrupted, refining prognosis and surgical need.
acgme: Peripheral Nerve Injury - Sunderland or Seddon Classification

concepts.name: Wallerian degeneration
concepts.blurb: Distal axon and myelin breakdown after transection, clearing the path for proximal regeneration.
acgme: Axonal Transport and Wallerian Degeneration

concepts.name: Axonal regeneration rate
concepts.blurb: Regenerating axons advance roughly 1 mm/day, setting realistic timelines for reinnervation and follow-up.
acgme: Axonal Transport and Wallerian Degeneration

concepts.name: Advancing Tinel sign
concepts.blurb: Percussion paresthesias that march distally over weeks, tracking the regenerating axon front.

concepts.name: Neuroma-in-continuity
concepts.blurb: Disorganized intraneural scar in an intact-appearing nerve; recovery hinges on conducting fascicles.

concepts.name: Timing of operative exploration
concepts.blurb: Sharp lacerations repaired immediately, blunt at 3 weeks, closed injuries observed 3-6 months for recovery.
acgme: Peripheral Nerve Injury - Sunderland or Seddon Classification

concepts.name: Intraoperative nerve action potential recording
concepts.blurb: Direct NAP across a neuroma-in-continuity guides neurolysis versus resection-and-graft decisions intraoperatively.

concepts.name: Double crush phenomenon
concepts.blurb: Proximal compression lowers threshold for symptomatic distal entrapment along the same axon.

concepts.name: EMG interpretation basics
concepts.blurb: Needle EMG distinguishes neurogenic from myopathic patterns and localizes the lesion by myotomal involvement.
acgme: EMG and Nerve Conduction Studies - Interpretation

concepts.name: Nerve conduction study basics
concepts.blurb: Amplitude reflects axon count, conduction velocity reflects myelin; localizes conduction block and demyelination.
acgme: EMG and Nerve Conduction Studies - Interpretation

concepts.name: Denervation and fibrillation timeline
concepts.blurb: Fibrillations and positive sharp waves appear about 2-3 weeks after axonal loss, not immediately.
acgme: EMG and Nerve Conduction Studies - Interpretation

concepts.name: When to obtain electrodiagnostics
concepts.blurb: Defer baseline EMG/NCS roughly 3-4 weeks post-injury so denervation changes are detectable.
acgme: EMG and Nerve Conduction Studies - Interpretation

concepts.name: MR neurography
concepts.blurb: High-resolution T2 nerve imaging shows fascicular detail, mass lesions, and denervation muscle signal.

concepts.name: High-resolution nerve ultrasound
concepts.blurb: Real-time imaging of nerve caliber, entrapment swelling, subluxation, and intraneural masses without radiation.

concepts.name: Carpal tunnel diagnosis
concepts.blurb: Median nerve compression at the wrist; nocturnal paresthesias with positive Phalen and Durkan compression tests.
acgme: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome - Diagnosis and Surgical Release

concepts.name: CTS electrodiagnostic severity grading
concepts.blurb: Graded mild-to-severe by distal latency prolongation, sensory loss, and axonal loss on EMG.
acgme: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome - Diagnosis and Surgical Release

concepts.name: Carpal tunnel release
concepts.blurb: Transverse carpal ligament division; open and endoscopic give equivalent outcomes with differing early recovery.
acgme: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome - Diagnosis and Surgical Release

concepts.name: Persistent or recurrent CTS
concepts.blurb: Incomplete ligament release, perineural scar, or misdiagnosis drives failure; revision needs confirmed pathology.
acgme: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome - Diagnosis and Surgical Release

concepts.name: Cubital tunnel syndrome diagnosis
concepts.blurb: Ulnar compression at the elbow; small-finger numbness, intrinsic weakness, positive elbow flexion test.
acgme: Cubital Tunnel Syndrome - Ulnar Nerve Decompression and Transposition

concepts.name: Cubital tunnel decompression vs transposition
concepts.blurb: Randomized data show in-situ decompression equals transposition with fewer complications absent subluxation.
acgme: Cubital Tunnel Syndrome - Ulnar Nerve Decompression and Transposition

concepts.name: Ulnar nerve at Guyon's canal
concepts.blurb: Wrist-level ulnar compression; zone determines motor, sensory, or mixed deficit sparing dorsal sensation.

concepts.name: Radial tunnel syndrome
concepts.blurb: Painful forearm radial nerve compression without motor loss; tenderness distal to lateral epicondyle.

concepts.name: Posterior interosseous nerve syndrome
concepts.blurb: Motor PIN palsy causing finger-drop with preserved wrist extension and no sensory loss.

concepts.name: Wartenberg syndrome
concepts.blurb: Superficial radial sensory nerve entrapment at the forearm; dorsoradial hand pain and numbness.

concepts.name: Pronator syndrome
concepts.blurb: Proximal median entrapment at the forearm with palmar cutaneous symptoms sparing nocturnal predominance.

concepts.name: Anterior interosseous nerve syndrome
concepts.blurb: Pure motor median branch palsy; weak FPL and index FDP yielding an abnormal pinch.

concepts.name: Common peroneal entrapment at fibular head
concepts.blurb: Compression at the fibular neck causing foot drop with weak dorsiflexion and eversion.
acgme: Lower Extremity Nerve Entrapment (Peroneal Tibial Tarsal Tunnel)

concepts.name: Tarsal tunnel syndrome
concepts.blurb: Posterior tibial nerve compression behind the medial malleolus causing burning plantar foot pain.
acgme: Lower Extremity Nerve Entrapment (Peroneal Tibial Tarsal Tunnel)

concepts.name: Meralgia paresthetica
concepts.blurb: Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve entrapment at the inguinal ligament; purely sensory lateral thigh burning.

concepts.name: Neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome
concepts.blurb: Lower-trunk/C8-T1 compression; true type has objective intrinsic wasting versus the common disputed type.
acgme: Thoracic Outlet Syndrome - Neurogenic and Vascular Types

concepts.name: Vascular thoracic outlet syndrome
concepts.blurb: Subclavian arterial or venous compression causing limb ischemia or effort thrombosis, not neural deficit.
acgme: Thoracic Outlet Syndrome - Neurogenic and Vascular Types

concepts.name: Suprascapular nerve entrapment
concepts.blurb: Compression at suprascapular or spinoglenoid notch; shoulder pain with infraspinatus or supraspinatus wasting.

concepts.name: Piriformis syndrome
concepts.blurb: Controversial deep-gluteal sciatic compression diagnosed by exclusion of lumbar radiculopathy and other causes.

concepts.name: Upper trunk Erb palsy
concepts.blurb: C5-C6 injury causing waiter's-tip posture with shoulder abduction and elbow flexion loss.
acgme: Brachial Plexus Injury - Anatomy Evaluation and Surgical Exploration

concepts.name: Lower trunk Klumpke palsy
concepts.blurb: C8-T1 injury producing intrinsic hand paralysis with claw hand and possible Horner syndrome.
acgme: Brachial Plexus Injury - Anatomy Evaluation and Surgical Exploration

concepts.name: Pan-plexopathy
concepts.blurb: Complete C5-T1 injury giving a flail anesthetic limb; high-energy traction with poor prognosis.
acgme: Brachial Plexus Injury - Anatomy Evaluation and Surgical Exploration

concepts.name: Preganglionic vs postganglionic injury
concepts.blurb: Distinction determines reconstructability; preganglionic root avulsion cannot be grafted and needs nerve transfer.
acgme: Brachial Plexus Injury - Anatomy Evaluation and Surgical Exploration

concepts.name: Root avulsion clinical signs
concepts.blurb: Horner syndrome, rhomboid/serratus weakness, and pseudomeningocele localize injury proximal to the dorsal root ganglion.
acgme: Brachial Plexus Injury - Anatomy Evaluation and Surgical Exploration

concepts.name: Brachial plexus injury imaging
concepts.blurb: CT myelography and MRI detect pseudomeningoceles and root avulsions guiding reconstruction strategy.
acgme: Brachial Plexus Injury - Anatomy Evaluation and Surgical Exploration

concepts.name: Oberlin nerve transfer
concepts.blurb: Fascicle of ulnar (and median) nerve to biceps motor branch restoring elbow flexion in upper-trunk injury.
acgme: Nerve Transfer Techniques for Reinnervation

concepts.name: Spinal accessory to suprascapular transfer
concepts.blurb: Distal spinal accessory neurotization of the suprascapular nerve restores shoulder abduction and external rotation.
acgme: Nerve Transfer Techniques for Reinnervation

concepts.name: Intercostal nerve transfer
concepts.blurb: Intercostal motor neurotization of biceps or free muscle when intraplexal donors are unavailable.
acgme: Nerve Transfer Techniques for Reinnervation

concepts.name: Timing of plexus reconstruction
concepts.blurb: Nerve transfers ideally within 6 months before motor endplates degenerate beyond reinnervation.
acgme: Adult and Pediatric Brachial Plexus Reconstruction

concepts.name: Free functional muscle transfer
concepts.blurb: Vascularized gracilis transfer with neurotization restores prehension in late or pan-plexus injuries.
acgme: Adult and Pediatric Brachial Plexus Reconstruction

concepts.name: Obstetric brachial plexus palsy
concepts.blurb: Birth traction injury; most Erb cases recover, with surgery indicated if biceps fails by 3-6 months.
acgme: Adult and Pediatric Brachial Plexus Reconstruction

concepts.name: Tension-free repair and gap principles
concepts.blurb: Coaptation must be tension-free; gaps beyond a few millimeters require grafting rather than mobilization.
acgme: Peripheral Nerve Repair and Grafting Principles

concepts.name: Direct epineurial repair
concepts.blurb: Primary epineurial neurorrhaphy aligning fascicles is preferred for sharp transections without a gap.
acgme: Peripheral Nerve Repair and Grafting Principles

concepts.name: Grouped fascicular repair
concepts.blurb: Group fascicle coaptation improves alignment in mixed nerves but adds intraneural dissection trauma.
acgme: Peripheral Nerve Repair and Grafting Principles

concepts.name: Sural nerve autograft
concepts.blurb: Gold-standard cable grafting donor bridging gaps; trades donor sensory loss for guided regeneration.
acgme: Peripheral Nerve Repair and Grafting Principles

concepts.name: Processed allograft and conduits
concepts.blurb: Acellular allografts and conduits bridge short sensory gaps, limited by length and diameter.
acgme: Peripheral Nerve Repair and Grafting Principles

concepts.name: End-to-side neurorrhaphy
concepts.blurb: Distal stump coapted to an intact donor side; sensory benefit clearer than debated motor recovery.
acgme: Peripheral Nerve Repair and Grafting Principles

concepts.name: Schwannoma
concepts.blurb: Encapsulated eccentric nerve sheath tumor displacing fascicles, enabling enucleation with fascicle preservation.
acgme: Peripheral Nerve Tumors (Schwannoma Neurofibroma) Resection

concepts.name: Neurofibroma
concepts.blurb: Unencapsulated tumor with fascicles coursing through it, making fascicle-sparing resection difficult.
acgme: Peripheral Nerve Tumors (Schwannoma Neurofibroma) Resection

concepts.name: Schwannoma enucleation
concepts.blurb: Epineurial window and microsurgical dissection shell out the tumor preserving surrounding functional fascicles.
acgme: Peripheral Nerve Tumors (Schwannoma Neurofibroma) Resection

concepts.name: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor
concepts.blurb: Rapid growth, pain, and new deficit signal malignancy; needs wide resection and adjuvant radiation.
acgme: Peripheral Nerve Tumors (Schwannoma Neurofibroma) Resection

concepts.name: NF1-associated plexiform neurofibroma
concepts.blurb: Diffuse multifascicular neurofibroma in NF1 carrying lifetime risk of malignant transformation.
acgme: Peripheral Nerve Tumors (Schwannoma Neurofibroma) Resection

concepts.name: Perineurioma
concepts.blurb: Benign perineurial cell tumor causing fusiform nerve enlargement and progressive motor mononeuropathy in young patients.

concepts.name: Intraneural ganglion cyst
concepts.blurb: Articular (synovial) theory explains joint-connected mucinous cysts tracking the peroneal nerve; ligate articular branch.

concepts.name: Parsonage-Turner syndrome
concepts.blurb: Idiopathic brachial neuritis with acute severe shoulder pain then patchy weakness, distinct from structural compression.

concepts.name: Foot drop differential
concepts.blurb: Peroneal palsy versus L5 radiculopathy: inversion strength and EMG of tibialis posterior discriminate the lesion.
acgme: Lower Extremity Nerve Entrapment (Peroneal Tibial Tarsal Tunnel)

concepts.name: Scapular winging differential
concepts.blurb: Medial winging from long thoracic/serratus versus lateral winging from spinal accessory/trapezius palsy.
